# Front differential locker installation

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove the front differential, cut out old rubber bushings and metal sleeves if necessary, then install new ones. [t2125]

Remove front crossmember and lift differential at an angle to insert bolts before swinging rear upward. [t2125]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the front crossmember from between the frame rails to create clearance.
2. Lift the differential into position at an angle, starting with the front end first.
3. Insert a bolt or pin through the front mount holes to temporarily hold the diff in place.
4. [Partial] Swing the rear of the differential upward and attach it back to the crossmember.
5. [Partial] Tighten all mounting bolts securely.

_Procedure reported by [t2125]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t2125] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the front differential from the vehicle.
2. Cut out or remove old rubber bushings and metal sleeves if necessary.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Lubricate drop bushings with grease before installation. [t2125]
- Use metric M12 bolts if standard 1/2-inch bolts do not align easily. [t2125]
- Use a boogie board under the lift point to stabilize heavy loads. [t2125]
- Loosen mounting bolts on bushings beforehand for wiggle room. [t2125]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Trying to install the diff with the crossmember fully seated without help or jacking points. [t2125]
- Forgetting that power applied forces a locker into engagement, causing wheel lock-up in 2WD if hubs are locked. [t2125]
